git 9bcfbb522 moved the reindex pass to a worker thread; 883d8af23 moved retrieval off-thread; neither changes the label rule
correct: The marker is printed when the bounded freshness wait (default 1.5 s) ends before the reindex pass finishes, OR when the pass failed. It does not compare against the index age, so on a catalog whose pass keeps exceeding the budget (or keeps failing) every call carries it, and a failed pass is labelled 'still running'. The results were not wrong; the label cannot tell fresh from stale. Workaround: set KB_FRESHNESS_BUDGET_MS (up to 60000) so the wait covers the pass; check the session log for '[kb] reindex failed'.

targets.text: Defect: freshnessStatus (reindex.ts) maps outcome 'failed' to the same STALE_LINE '(index refresh still running ...)' as 'timeout', and the line is shown on every call while passes keep timing out. Expected: distinct text for failed ('last refresh failed') vs running, and no marker once a pass has completed since the last file change. Workaround: KB_FRESHNESS_BUDGET_MS.

correct: A fresh database is created only from the model's generated Liquibase changelog; hand-written changesets (the migration version folder, updateDataAfterIncremental) run only in the upgrade path, so no changeset hook exists on creation. Foreign-key indexes are not generated (only identifier attributes get an index). They must be applied outside the model, e.g. a SQL script run after the first start of a new database.

targets.heading: When No Manual Step Is Needed
targets.text: A fresh database runs only the generated model changelog: hand-written changesets in the migration version folder (including `updateDataAfterIncremental`) run only when an existing database is upgraded, and there is no hook that runs a changeset on creation. Objects the model cannot express (for example indexes on foreign-key columns, which the generator never creates) therefore have to be applied to every new database by a script outside the model, run after the first start created the tables (for example `psql -f <script>.sql`).

targets.heading: 12. Foreign-key columns get no index
targets.text: Add to Behaviour: a fresh database has no hook for hand-written changesets either (SimpleLiquibaseExecutor.executueOnLiquibaseModel runs only the serialized model changelog), so a manual index script is unavoidable per new database. Expected: generate FK indexes, or run a project changelog after the model changelog on creation.

note: Issue 12 already exists in FRAMEWORK.md; only an addendum is proposed.

correct: ./judo.sh start (karaf runtime) starts PostgreSQL, Keycloak and Karaf; the compose environments start traefik, Keycloak, the app and the database. Neither starts an SMTP server or mail catcher. JUDO_PLATFORM_LOG_SMTP_SERVER=true in the compose files is a logging flag (log the SMTP server), not a server. Mail-reading specs need a catcher the project provides itself on the configured SMTP host/port.

targets.heading: Runtime Issues
targets.text:
#### No mails arrive / `ECONNREFUSED` on the SMTP port

##### Solution
- `./judo.sh start` and the template's compose environments start no SMTP server or mail catcher (`JUDO_PLATFORM_LOG_SMTP_SERVER=true` only enables logging). Run one yourself, for example `docker run -d --name <app>-mail -p 1025:1025 -p 8025:8025 axllent/mailpit`, and point the SMTP variables of [Email (SMTP)](../backend/application-config.md) at it. A stopped container is removed by `docker system prune`; recreate it with the same command.

note: Mailpit is only an example of a catcher; the template does not name one.

correct: The route is given but written wrongly: the generated route is GET /api/<Model>/<Actor>/<Actor>/~principal (applicationPath '<Model>/<Actor>' plus method path '/<Actor>/~principal'), e.g. /api/webshop/Customer/Customer/~principal, not '/Actor/<Actor>/'. A direct data call such as ~list answers 403 AUTHENTICATED_ENTITY_NOT_FOUND for a new user because a provisioning interceptor that filters on '#_principal' (as the pattern does) never runs for it. A script provisions the user by calling GET .../~principal with the bearer token once before the data calls.

targets.heading: Discovery endpoints for custom frontends
targets.text:
#### Provisioning a new user from a script

An interceptor that filters on `#_principal` runs only for that call. A data call (`.../~list`) with a new user's token answers 403 `AUTHENTICATED_ENTITY_NOT_FOUND` and creates no row. Call `GET /api/<Model>/<Actor>/<Actor>/~principal` with the bearer token once first (the generated frontend does this); the interceptor then creates the row and later calls succeed.

note: Whether the segment after the actor is always the actor name was seen only in the generated webshop code (Admin and Customer). Second-order claim in the item (first call fails, second works neither) is consistent: no #_principal call was made. Not reproduced live (needs running stack).

correct: karaf_port/keycloak_port/postgres_port work only with runtime=karaf (the default local start). A different port works for the browser login because the generated Keycloak clients accept any redirect URI ('*'); web origins depend on the configured CORS allow-origin. The generated Playwright config reads APP_URL (default http://localhost:8181), so e2e against another port needs APP_URL=http://localhost:<port>. keycloak_port conflicts (8080) are fixed the same way (-o keycloak_port=<port>); the docs line only names karaf_port.

targets.heading: "Port 8181 (or 8080) already in use"
targets.replaces: - Stop the conflicting service or start with another port: `./judo.sh start -o karaf_port=<port>`
targets.text:
- Stop the conflicting service or start with another port: `./judo.sh start -o karaf_port=<port>` (Karaf, default 8181), `-o keycloak_port=<port>` (Keycloak, default 8080), `-o postgres_port=<port>` (PostgreSQL, default 5432); combine with commas. These options apply to the default `runtime=karaf`, not to the compose environments.
- The browser login works on another Karaf port because the generated Keycloak clients allow any redirect URI (`*`). Run Playwright against it with `APP_URL=http://localhost:<port>` (the generated config defaults to `http://localhost:8181`).

note: webOrigins '*' not verified as generator default; stated as configuration dependent.
